Part A
# A.
```{r}
shoes <-  data.frame(
          ShoeSize = c(6.5, 9.0, 8.5, 8.5, 10.5, 7.0, 9.5, 9.0, 13.0, 7.5, 10.5, 8.5, 12.0, 10.5,
                      13.0, 11.5, 8.5, 5.0, 10.0, 6.5, 7.5, 8.5, 10.5, 8.5, 10.5, 11.0, 9.0, 13.0),
          Height   = c(66.0, 68.0, 64.5, 65.0, 70.0, 64.0, 70.0, 71.0, 72.0, 64.0, 74.5, 67.0, 71.0, 71.0,
                      77.0, 72.0, 59.0, 62.0, 72.0, 66.0, 64.0, 67.0, 73.0, 69.0, 72.0, 70.0, 69.0, 70.0),
          Gender   = c("F", "F", "F", "F", "M", "F", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M", "F", "M", "M",
                      "M", "M", "F", "F", "M", "F", "F", "M", "M", "F", "M", "M", "M", "M")
                    )
write.csv(shoes, "shoesize.csv", row.names = FALSE )
```

```{r}
females
```
#It organizes them by gender.

# Question 7
```{r}
males   <- subset(shoes, Gender == "M")
females <- subset(shoes, Gender == "F")

mean(males$Height);   mean(females$Height)
mean(males$ShoeSize); mean(females$ShoeSize)
```
#Males generally have both higher average heights and larger average shoe sizes compared to females.

#Yes its important, Gender plays a big role here. The strong link between shoe size and height is mostly because males are generally taller and have larger feet than females.
